claim: YouTube Partner Program eligibility is a disjunction of two paths: 1,000 subscribers plus 4,000 valid public watch hours in the trailing 12 months, OR 1,000 subscribers plus 10 million valid public Shorts views in the trailing 90 days.
scope_conditions: Global YouTube Partner Program policy as of fetch date 27 July 2026; excludes 'expanded YPP' countries which have a lower fan-funding-only tier
quoted_support: Get 1,000 subscribers with 4,000 valid public watch hours in the last 12 months, or Get 1,000 subscribers with 10 million valid public Shorts views in the last 90 days.

claim: Watch hours earned from Shorts views in the Shorts Feed do not count toward the 4,000-hour long-form threshold, so the two eligibility paths are mutually exclusive counting systems, not additive.
quoted_support: Keep in mind that any public watch hours from Shorts views in the Shorts Feed won't count towards the 4,000 public watch hours threshold.

claim: Meeting the numeric YPP threshold does not automatically confer monetization; every eligible channel enters a manual/automated review queue with a stated typical decision time of about one month, meaning time-to-first-income includes an application-review lag beyond the time needed to accumulate subscribers/watch hours.
stance_target: time from starting to first meaningful income is longer than the raw subscriber/watch-hour threshold implies
quoted_support: We'll get back to you with a decision once your channel is reviewed (typically in about 1 month).

claim: Rejected YPP applicants face a structured cooling-off/reapplication ladder: appeal within 21 days, or reapply after 30 days on first rejection, escalating to a 90-day wait after a repeat rejection.
stance_target: time-to-first-income delays for creators who fail initial review
scope_conditions: global YPP applicants who are rejected
quoted_support: you can appeal the decision within 21 days or keep uploading original content and you'll be able to re-apply after a 30-day period... if you've previously re-applied, you can try again after a 90-day period.

claim: YouTube operationalizes a formal inactivity-based exit rule for monetized channels: monetization may be turned off for any channel that has not uploaded a video or posted to the Posts tab for 6 months or more, independent of subscriber/watch-hour counts.
stance_target: platform-disclosed operational definition of creator attrition/exit for monetized channels
scope_conditions: global, applies to any monetized (YPP) channel
quoted_support: we may turn off monetization on channels that haven't uploaded a video or posted to the Posts tab for 6 months or more

claim: Six non-numeric prerequisites gate YPP entry beyond the subscriber/watch-hour or Shorts-view threshold: compliance with monetization policies, residence in an eligible country/region, no active Community Guidelines strikes, 2-Step Verification enabled, advanced-features access, and a linked AdSense for YouTube account.
stance_target: full description of the monetization eligibility gate
quoted_support: Follow the YouTube channel monetization policies... Live in a country/region where the YouTube Partner Program is available... Have no active Community Guidelines strikes... 2-Step Verification is turned on... Have advanced features access... Have one active AdSense for YouTube account linked.

claim: Channels that drop below the subscriber/watch-hour threshold after applying are still reviewed for YPP -- the threshold is a one-time gate to enter the review queue, not a continuously re-verified condition prior to acceptance.
quoted_support: So it doesn't matter if your subscriber or watch hour counts drop below the threshold while waiting for review. If you've met the threshold and applied for YPP, we'll still review your channel for YPP suitability.

claim: This eligibility page discloses no data on how many applicant channels are accepted vs. rejected, no distribution of time-to-approval beyond the single 'about 1 month' typical figure, and no data on what accepted channels subsequently earn -- the page describes only the eligibility gate mechanism, not outcomes.
stance_target: absence of creator-level earnings/acceptance-rate distribution in platform disclosure
scope_conditions: scope limited to this specific YouTube Help page
quoted_support: N/A -- absence noted by the fetcher after full read of the page; no acceptance-rate, rejection-rate, or post-acceptance earnings figures appear anywhere in the document.
